description: STATE SAFETY: the change gate DENIES terraform apply on production — mutation is a separate authority the agent cannot exercise
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform -chdir=infra/environments/prod apply"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo denied || echo allowed

description: STATE SAFETY: terraform plan on production is ALLOWED — planning is read-only, only apply is gated
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform -chdir=infra/environments/prod plan"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo allowed || echo denied

description: PLAN ANALYSIS: a plan of pure creates (the known-good plan) analyzes to verdict 'clean' — nothing destroyed, nothing replaced
BLAST RADIUS: the good plan touches all 31 resources — the analyzer reports the count a reviewer would gate on
STATEFUL REPLACE: the plan that recreates the RDS instance analyzes to 'block' — a stateful replacement is a data-loss risk, not a routine change
STATEFUL REPLACE: the analyzer names the exact resource being destroyed and recreated — the database, so the finding is actionable
SECURITY SCAN: the plan adding a 0.0.0.0/0 rule scans to 'block' — an internet-open ingress on a datastore port is a page-the-team finding
SENSITIVE EXPOSURE: the scan pinpoints the rule opening Postgres (5432) to the whole internet — the datastore, not a web tier
SECURITY SCAN: the good plan has no wide-open or public exposure — verdict 'clean', so the scan does not cry wolf
COST ESTIMATION: the oversize change is a +$2847/mo delta over baseline — the number that turns a sizing choice into a budget decision
FINOPS THRESHOLD: a per-resource cost jump past 2x (the RDS instance grows 16x) blocks — the FinOps role's 'flag changes > 2x' rule, enforced
ENVIRONMENT DRIFT: diffing the candidate against the known-good baseline surfaces the NEW 0.0.0.0/0 rule that drifted in — verdict 'block'
ROLLBACK REVIEW: the stateful-replace plan is judged irreversible — its approval REQUIRES a restore-from-backup plan, it is not a clean roll back
ROLLBACK REVIEW: a pure-create plan is reversible (destroy what you made) — verdict 'approve', no restore plan needed
AUTHORITY: the IaC engineer STRUCTURALLY carries a write tool — authoring HCL is in its role (exit 0)
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh iac-engineer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo capable || echo blocked

description: AUTHORITY: the FinOps analyst CANNOT write — it reads plans and prices them, it does not mutate infrastructure (exit 3)
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh finops-analyst write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo blocked || echo capable

description: AGENT-RUN COST RECEIPT: the mixed-model handoff chain is cheaper than running every role on opus — right-sizing the model per role is itself a FinOps decision
HANDOFF CHAIN: the good plan clears all four stages (IaC -> Security -> FinOps -> Change Reviewer) and the pipeline verdict is 'approve'
HANDOFF CHAIN: one stage's block stops the line — the stateful-replace plan is blocked by the pipeline even though its syntax is valid
FAIL-CLOSED: handed a file that is not a plan JSON, the analyzer refuses (exit 1) rather than emit a made-up verdict
command: scripts/plan-analyze.sh infra/versions.tf --field verdict >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: STYLE SKILL: the terraform-style skill exists — the house conventions are a written artifact the agent is held to, not a habit in one engineer's head
YOUR MODULE: the read-replica module exists with the three-file layout the estate uses (main/variables/outputs)
YOUR MODULE: terraform fmt reports no diff — the generated HCL matches canonical formatting
command: terraform -chdir=infra/modules/read-replica fmt -check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo clean || echo unformatted

description: HOUSE STYLE: the replica resource carries a role noun, not the generic 'this' — the estate names its primary resource for what it is
command: M=infra/modules/read-replica/main.tf; [ -f $M ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'resource "aws_db_instance" "this"' $M && echo generic || echo role-named

description: HOUSE STYLE: the replica identifier is interpolated from project+environment, not hardcoded — the module survives being reused in another environment
command: grep -Eq 'identifier[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"\$\{var\.project\}-\$\{var\.environment\}' infra/modules/read-replica/main.tf 2>/dev/null && echo interpolated || echo hardcoded

description: SECURITY BASELINE: storage_encrypted is true in the module source — the baseline the security scan does NOT check, caught at authoring time by the style skill
command: grep -Eq 'storage_encrypted[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*true' infra/modules/read-replica/main.tf 2>/dev/null && echo encrypted || echo unencrypted

description: SECURITY BASELINE: publicly_accessible is false — a datastore replica is never reachable from the internet, and Step 8 restored this after breaking it
command: M=infra/modules/read-replica/main.tf; [ -f $M ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -Eq 'publicly_accessible[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*true' $M && echo public || echo private

description: HOUSE STYLE: every output carries a description — an undocumented output is an undocumented API
command: O=infra/modules/read-replica/outputs.tf; [ -f $O ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; n=$(grep -c '^output' $O); d=$(grep -c 'description' $O); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" = "$d" ] && echo described || echo undocumented

description: SECURITY: no literal password or secret string in the module source — secrets arrive as sensitive variables
command: M=infra/modules/read-replica; [ -f $M/main.tf ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -Eiq '(password|secret)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"[^"$]' $M/*.tf && echo literal-secret || echo clean

description: YOUR PLAN: the plan generated from YOUR module analyzes to 'clean' — a pure-create change with nothing destroyed or replaced
YOUR PLAN: the security scan clears YOUR plan — the module you shipped has no public exposure, after you broke it in Step 8 and put it back
